newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: MEMORIAL SERVICE FOR MURDERED SYDNEY CONSTABLE
A memorial service will be held today for murdered Sydney police officer David Carty.
The 25-year old constable died after being stabbed in the chest during a fight outside a hotel at Fairfield in Sydney's west.
The service will be held at the Liverpool Catholic Church this morning.
Two men are expected to appear in court today charged with murdering the off-duty officer.
24-year old Ashur Darmo and 30-year old Amir Dankha were refused bail when they appeared in Paramatta Court yesterday.
Police have so far arrested and charged five-people over Constable Carty's killing.
NO NEGOTIATED SETTLEMENT ON WIK SAYS LIBERAL PRESIDENT
Queensland Liberal Party President, Bob Tucker, says it's clear there won't be a negotiated settlement on native title.
His comment comes as the Prime Minister prepares to meet Aboriginal negotiators today before finalising the Government's position on native title, following the High Court's Wik decision.
Indigenous leaders have threatened to push for international trade sanctions against Australia if native title is wiped out.
But the conservative parties in Queensland, Western Australia and the Northern Territory are urging Mr Howard not to bow to the threats.
Mr Tucker has told ABC Radio the Prime Minister's next step is to finalise a legislative solution and put it into effect.
POLICE SEARCH FOR MAN WANTED OVER LIBRARIAN'S SHOOTING
Police in Sydney are continuing the search for a 46-year old man wanted for questioning over the shooting death of a high school librarian.
Irene Davis was shot early yesterday morning as she returned to her Cronulla home, in Sydney's south, from a night out.
Police want to question 46-year old Russel John Meyer over Mrs Davis' death.

Meanwhile, detectives are hoping a post mortem examination today will reveal the cause of death of a man whose body was found in a dam at the Steelworks golf course in the Newcastle suburb of Shortland yesterday.
Detectives believe the body may have been dumped in the dam on Saturday night and are waiting on the results of the autopsy to determine whether the man was murdered.
A group of golfers found the body.
MAN DROWNS AT WOLLONGONG
A Victorian man has drowned while trying to save his son at a northern Wollongong beach.
Edward Moses, 46, from Melbourne, got caught in a rip yesterday afternoon while attempting to rescue his son at the unpatrolled Poverty Beach.
The boy made it back to shore, but his father was found face down in the water by a fisherman about 15 minutes later.
Attempts to revive him failed.
The family were holidaying in the area.
Meanwhile, a woman has died and three others were injured in an accident last night in the centre of Kiama.
The woman was a passenger in a ute which collided with a car at around six o'clock.
A motor-cyclist was airlifted to Sydney this morning for micro-surgery after colliding with a truck at Macquarie Pass last night.
The man lost control on a bend and slid under the back-wheel of the semi-trailer, partially severing an arm.
SEARCH FOR THREE IN TORRES STRAIT
An air and sea search resumed at first light for three people missing since Friday night, after their dinghy overturned in the Torres Strait.
The Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre says five people were on board the dinghy when it overturned en route from Mabuag Island to Horn Island.
Two women were able to swim to Spencer Island where they raised the alarm yesterday morning.
A search yesterday involving 9 aircraft, failed to locate the two adults and a child.
Local volunteer boats will also join the search.
Meanwhile, investigations will continue this morning into the circumstances leading to reports that two women fell overboard from a merchant vessel off the Far north Queensland coast.
The Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre says the women were reported mising on Saturday from the Malayasian vessel in Princess Charlotte Bay.
A search yesterday by six aircraft failed to locate them.
Police and Immigration Department officials are investigating the possibility that the two women in their twenties are still on the boat.
UNION SAYS JOBS MAY GO AND CHARGES MAY GO UP AT TELSTRA
The Communications Union says the result of Telstra's three-billon dollar dividend to the Federal Government, will be raised charges and lost jobs.
Union President Colin Cooper says the loan Telstra has to take out to fund the dividend will mean a cutback in its capital works program, affecting jobs in the manufacturing area.
Mr Cooper says either jobs will be lost, particularly in Ericssons and Alcatel, or Telstra will have to raise charges, affecting consumers.
SA LABOR PARTY CALLS FOR TERRITORY STATEHOOD TO BE ON AGENDA
The South Australian Labor party is calling for Northern Territory statehood to be on the agenda of the Constitutional Convention, in December.
Labor leader Mike Rann wants the issue linked to a commitment from the Federal Government to build the Adelaide to Darwin rail-link.
He says South Australia gave up the Northern Territory in 1912, on the condition that the Adelaide to Darwin rail-link was built.
Mr Rann says it's time that commitment is met, and the railway should be the Northern Teritory's "bridge to statehood".
OPPOSITION SAYS SENATE INQUIRY INTO COLSTON OK
Federal Government claims a Senate inquiry would interfere with a Federal Police investigation into Senator Mal Colston's use of travel expenses have been dismissed by the Opposition.
The Opposition's released advice from Clerk of the Senate, Harry Evans, that a Senate inquiry wouldn't create insurmountable difficulties for the Police investigation or any subsequent court case.
The Government claims a Senate Privileges Committee investigation could prejudice any future prosecution of Senator Colston.
Mr Evans says the two investigations are about different issues.
He says a Senate Inquiry's into the truthfulness of statements made to it by Senator Colston and his office manager, while the police would investigate whether the travel claims constitute fraud.
